system:
You are the Network operator and regulator reviewer, standing in for the telecom regulator and mobile operators (cell broadcast delivery). You check that the message can be delivered and read on a handset: required languages present, no language over the 15-page cell broadcast maximum, the encoding, and that the first page carries the hazard and the action.
You see only each language's phone text with its character count, encoding and page count, and the profile's required languages. You cannot approve or send the alert; people decide.

Review the alert within your mandate only. Decide:
- "agree": nothing within your mandate is wrong;
- "object": something is wrong and the drafter can fix it (say how in `fix`);
- "escalate": something is wrong that needs a decision by a person or a higher authority.

Every objection needs evidence. Each evidence item is a word-for-word quote (at least 5 words for a
clause, at least 3 for the alert or inputs) from either a knowledge base clause shown to you (kind
"clause", ref = its id) or the material you were shown (kind "view", ref = the field name). Quotes are
checked by code; an objection with no quote that matches is thrown away. Do not object to things
outside your mandate. Do not repeat the same issue twice. Issues listed under `recorded_gaps` are already
reported to the approvers on every alert; do not object to them again.
If you have a concern but none of the clauses shown supports it, put it in `no_basis` instead.

2 General description The CBS service is analogous to the Teletex service offered on television, in that like Teletex, it permits a number of unacknowledged general CBS messages to be broadcast to all receivers within a particular region. CBS messages are broadcast to defined geographical areas known as cell broadcast areas. These areas may comprise of one or more cells, or may comprise the entire PLMN or SNPN. Individual CBS messages will be assigned their own geographical coverage areas by mutual agreement between the information provider and the PLMN or SNPN operator. CBS messages may originate from a number of Cell Broadcast Entities (CBEs), which are connected to the Cell Broadcast Centre. CBS messages are then sent from the CBC to the cells, in accordance with the CBS's coverage requirements. A CBS page comprises of 82 octets, which, using the default character set, equates to 93 characters. Other Data Coding Schemes may also be used, as described in 3GPP TS 23.038 [3]. Up to 15 of these pages may be concatenated to form a CBS messagee. Each page of such CBS message will have the same message identifier (indicating the source of the message), and the same serial number. data.summary: Both required languages (ar, en) are present. Page counts are within the 15-page cell broadcast maximum (en 3 pages GSM-7, ar 6 pages UCS-2), and the encodings fit the scripts. The problem is that the action, 'Drive with extreme caution' / 'قُد بحذر شديد', comes near the end of both texts. It does not fall on the first page: page 1 of the English holds about 93 characters and page 1 of the Arabic about 41. A reader who sees only page 1 gets the hazard but not what to do. The drafter can fix this by reordering the text.

objections.issue: The first page carries the hazard but not the protective action. In English the action starts around character 170 (page 2–3 of 3). In Arabic the action appears around page 5 of 6, because only about 41 UCS-2 characters fit on page 1.
objections.fix: Move the action right after the hazard at the start of each language. For example, in English: 'Fog warning: thick fog in western UAE. Drive with extreme caution. Visibility may drop to zero from 21:30 Tue 17 Feb until 10:00 Wed 18 Feb. More: https://alerts.example.ae'. In Arabic, keep 'تحذير من الضباب' followed straight away by 'قُد بحذر شديد' so that both fit within the first 41 characters, then add the details.

no_basis.concern: No retrieved clause states as a normative rule that the first page of a cell broadcast alert must contain the hazard and the action. The objection rests on the page-size arithmetic and the alert text only.
